audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for weakness/trembling, Spirit and power, hidden wisdom, Spirit searching depths, spiritual discernment, mind of Messiah.

verses.restored: And I, coming to you, siblings, did not come according to superiority of word or wisdom, announcing to you the mystery/testimony of the Divine.

familiar.text: And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of God.

modern.text: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.

original.text: Κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, ἦλθον οὐ καθʼ ὑπεροχὴν λόγου ἢ σοφίας καταγγέλλων ὑμῖν τὸ ⸀μαρτύριον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Messiah, and him crucified.

familiar.text: For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

modern.text: For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.

original.text: οὐ γὰρ ἔκρινά ⸂τι εἰδέναι⸃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυρωμένον·

verses.restored: And I was with you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling.

familiar.text: And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.

modern.text: I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling.

original.text: κἀγὼ ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ καὶ ἐν φόβῳ καὶ ἐν τρόμῳ πολλῷ ἐγενόμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς,

verses.restored: My word and my proclamation were not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in demonstration of Spirit and power,

familiar.text: And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power:

modern.text: My message and my preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power,

original.text: καὶ ὁ λόγος μου καὶ τὸ κήρυγμά μου οὐκ ἐν ⸂πειθοῖ σοφίας⸃ ἀλλʼ ἐν ἀποδείξει πνεύματος καὶ δυνάμεως,

verses.restored: so that your trust might not be in human wisdom but in power of the Divine.

familiar.text: That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

modern.text: so that your faith would not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power. Spiritual Wisdom (Ephesians 1:15–23)

original.text: ἵνα ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν μὴ ᾖ ἐν σοφίᾳ ἀνθρώπων ἀλλʼ ἐν δυνάμει θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Yet we speak wisdom among the mature/complete, but not wisdom of this age nor of rulers of this age who are being made inactive.

familiar.text: Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought:

modern.text: Among the mature, however, we speak a message of wisdom—but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.

original.text: Σοφίαν δὲ λαλοῦμεν ἐν τοῖς τελείοις, σοφίαν δὲ οὐ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου οὐδὲ τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου τῶν καταργουμένων·

verses.restored: But we speak Divine wisdom in mystery, hidden, which the Divine marked out beforehand before the ages for our glory,

familiar.text: But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory:

modern.text: No, we speak of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God, which He destined for our glory before time began.

original.text: ἀλλὰ λαλοῦμεν ⸂θεοῦ σοφίαν⸃ ἐν μυστηρίῳ, τὴν ἀποκεκρυμμένην, ἣν προώρισεν ὁ θεὸς πρὸ τῶν αἰώνων εἰς δόξαν ἡμῶν·

verses.restored: which none of the rulers of this age has known; for if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

familiar.text: Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

modern.text: None of the rulers of this age understood it. For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

original.text: ἣν οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἔγνωκεν, εἰ γὰρ ἔγνωσαν, οὐκ ἂν τὸν κύριον τῆς δόξης ἐσταύρωσαν·

verses.restored: But just as it is written: What eye did not see and ear did not hear and did not rise upon the human heart, what the Divine prepared for those loving him.

familiar.text: But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.

modern.text: Rather, as it is written: “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him.”

original.text: ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἃ ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν καὶ οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν καὶ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἀνέβη, ⸀ὅσα ἡτοίμασεν ὁ θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: For to us the Divine unveiled these things through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of the Divine.

familiar.text: But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.

modern.text: But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit. The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.

original.text: ἡμῖν ⸀γὰρ ⸂ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ θεὸς⸃ διὰ τοῦ ⸀πνεύματος, τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα πάντα ἐραυνᾷ, καὶ τὰ βάθη τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: For who among humans knows the things of a human except the spirit of the human within? So also the things of the Divine no one has known except the Spirit of the Divine.

familiar.text: For what man knoweth the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God.

modern.text: For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.

original.text: τίς γὰρ οἶδεν ἀνθρώπων τὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ; οὕτως καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐδεὶς ⸀ἔγνωκεν εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: But we did not receive the spirit of the world, but the Spirit from the Divine, so that we may know the things graciously given to us by the Divine.

familiar.text: Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God.

modern.text: We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.

original.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ κόσμου ἐλάβομεν ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα εἰδῶμεν τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ χαρισθέντα ἡμῖν·

verses.restored: These things we also speak, not in taught words of human wisdom, but in taught words of Spirit, interpreting spiritual things to spiritual ones.

familiar.text: Which things also we speak, not in the words which man’s wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

modern.text: And this is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words.

original.text: ἃ καὶ λαλοῦμεν οὐκ ἐν διδακτοῖς ἀνθρωπίνης σοφίας λόγοις, ἀλλʼ ἐν διδακτοῖς ⸀πνεύματος, πνευματικοῖς πνευματικὰ συγκρίνοντες.

verses.restored: But the natural/soul-level human does not receive the things of the Spirit of the Divine, for they are foolishness to that one, and one is not able to know them, because they are spiritually discerned.

familiar.text: But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.

modern.text: The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.

original.text: Ψυχικὸς δὲ ἄνθρωπος οὐ δέχεται τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ θεοῦ, μωρία γὰρ αὐτῷ ἐστίν, καὶ οὐ δύναται γνῶναι, ὅτι πνευματικῶς ἀνακρίνεται·

verses.restored: The spiritual one discerns all things, but is discerned by no one.

familiar.text: But he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man.

modern.text: The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment.

original.text: ὁ δὲ πνευματικὸς ἀνακρίνει ⸀τὰ πάντα, αὐτὸς δὲ ὑπʼ οὐδενὸς ἀνακρίνεται.

verses.restored: For who has known the mind of the Lord, who will instruct him? But we have the mind of Messiah.

familiar.text: For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.

modern.text: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.

original.text: τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου, ὃς συμβιβάσει αὐτόν; ἡμεῖς δὲ νοῦν Χριστοῦ ἔχομεν.

translation_notes: Psychikos is rendered natural/soul-level to preserve the contrast with pneumatikos/spiritual without implying the soul is evil.
Paul rejects status-performance wisdom, not deep wisdom itself; he speaks hidden Divine wisdom through Spirit.
